parameters.content:
## W1b - Backfill contacts on existing prospects

Companion to W1. W1's dedupe is permanent and by domain: once a company is in
`sanaku_prospects`, W1 will never look at it again, even after Apollo people
search comes back online. That leaves the whole existing backlog stuck at
"business-only" (Google Places, no named contact) forever - W1 alone can
never fix rows it already wrote.

This workflow closes that gap. Per run:
1. Pull existing prospects with no named contact (`contact_name IS NULL`,
   `source = 'google_places'`, `status = 'new'`, not do-not-contact),
   best first (Tier 1 before Tier 2/3, highest intent first), capped at
   `maxRevealsPerRun` - the same budget name and meaning as W1's, just
   spent against the backlog instead of fresh discoveries.
2. Per company: Apollo people search SCOPED TO ITS DOMAIN
   (`q_organization_domains_list`) - both passes, seniority then ops-title,
   same authority ranking as W1's Filter & Dedupe (kept in sync by hand -
   no shared code between separate workflow files). Search is free.
3. Best-ranked person found -> reveal (paid: ~1 credit email, 8 credits
   phone - phone only for the front of the same list, same as W1). Update
   the EXISTING row in place - never a new row, never touching its score,
   tier, or tech signals. Phone reveal is async exactly like W1's: this
   only kicks it off (`phone_reveal_request_id`), and W1's own
   'Get Pending Phone Reveals' side-branch resolves it on its next run,
   whichever workflow set the pending id.
4. Nobody found for a company -> row is left untouched. Not every business
   has anyone in Apollo; this is a normal, common, unlogged outcome, not
   a failure (matches W1: company-level zero results are routine).

Meant to be run on demand against the backlog, not on a weekly schedule -
trigger via Manual Trigger in the editor, or the `sanaku-run-w1b-backfill`
webhook GET. Uses the SAME Apollo/Supabase credentials as W1, and the SAME
env-driven install pattern: `sh ~/sanaku.sh import w1b-backfill-contacts`
turns Apollo on/off and sizes the reveal budgets exactly like W1's import
does, because this file's Run Config node uses the identical
useApollo / maxRevealsPerRun / maxPhoneRevealsPerRun field names the
installer's generic patcher already knows how to rewrite.

If a run does nothing, check `sh ~/sanaku.sh status` for a
'Apollo backfill skipped: useApollo is false' line - that means no
APOLLO_KEY was present when this was last imported, so re-import with the
key set: `sh ~/sanaku.sh import w1b-backfill-contacts`.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ workflow: $workflow.name, error: 'Apollo backfill skipped: useApollo is false - no APOLLO_KEY was configured when this workflow was last imported. Re-import with the key set: sh ~/sanaku.sh import w1b-backfill-contacts', payload: {} }) }}
={{ JSON.stringify({ q_organization_domains_list: [$json.domain], person_seniorities: $('Run Config').first().json.personSeniorities, per_page: 10, page: 1 }) }}

={{ JSON.stringify({ workflow: $workflow.name, error: 'Apollo backfill search failed: ' + String(($json.error && $json.error.message) || 'unknown').slice(0, 1000), payload: { domain: $('Per Backfill Candidate').first().json.domain, vertical: $('Per Backfill Candidate').first().json.vertical } }) }}

={{ JSON.stringify({ q_organization_domains_list: [$('Per Backfill Candidate').first().json.domain], person_titles: ($('Run Config').first().json.opsTitles[$('Per Backfill Candidate').first().json.vertical] || []), per_page: 10, page: 1 }) }}

={{ JSON.stringify({ workflow: $workflow.name, error: 'Apollo backfill ops search failed: ' + String(($json.error && $json.error.message) || 'unknown').slice(0, 1000), payload: { domain: $('Per Backfill Candidate').first().json.domain, vertical: $('Per Backfill Candidate').first().json.vertical } }) }}

={{ JSON.stringify({ id: $json.apollo_person_id, reveal_personal_emails: true, reveal_phone_number: $json.needsPhoneReveal === true, webhook_url: $env.DASHBOARD_URL + '/apollo-phone-reveal-noop' }) }}

={{ JSON.stringify({ contact_name: $json.contact_name, contact_title: $json.contact_title, contact_authority: $json.contact_authority, decision_maker: $json.decision_maker, contact_email: $json.contact_email, contact_email_personal: $json.contact_email_personal, contact_linkedin_url: $json.contact_linkedin_url, phone_reveal_request_id: $json.phone_reveal_request_id, phone_reveal_requested_at: $json.phone_reveal_requested_at }) }}
